findings.title: Run enabled with a probe/source not valid for the current mode
findings.message: In ac-gain mode the probe options are filtered to `v:` probes, but `ProbeID` keeps any earlier selection, such as a current probe from dc mode. Run stays enabled and the selector's `SelectedID` may not match any of its options. The source selector has the same problem when `SourceID` is not a listed non-battery voltage source. The run then fails on the server, or the view may fail validation.
findings.suggestion: Disable Run, or prompt for a new selection, when `p.ProbeID` is not among the `probes` options. In ac-gain mode, also require `p.SourceID` to be among the `sources` options.

findings.title: Progress uses live settings instead of the running job's trial count
findings.message: The progress denominator comes from the current settings (`p.Trials`), not from the run in progress. Native controls are disabled while busy, but an agent can still call `tolerance.settings.set` mid-run. After that, the display can show a misleading count such as "12 / 4 trials".
findings.suggestion: Show the trial count captured for the active run, for example a run-settings or total field on `ToleranceState`, instead of the live settings.
findings.evidence: nodes = append(nodes, quiet("tolerance-progress", fmt.Sprintf("%s · %d / %d trials", v.Status, v.Completed, p.Trials)), s.action("tolerance-cancel", "Cancel tolerance run", "tolerance.cancel", workbench.IDParams{ID: v.ID}))

findings.title: CSV formula escaping misses leading tab/CR triggers
findings.message: `toleranceCSVText` escapes cells whose first non-whitespace character is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. A leading tab or carriage return can also make spreadsheets interpret a cell, and OWASP lists both as formula-injection triggers. A cell such as `\t...` is only prefixed if `=+-@` follows the whitespace, so the protection is incomplete. Failure messages can contain user-authored component or probe IDs.
findings.suggestion: Also prefix any cell whose first character is a tab or carriage return.

findings.title: Progress counter may race and the exact-count assertion is brittle
findings.message: The test asserts that the progress callback runs exactly once. If `computeTolerance` evaluates trials concurrently or reports progress from worker goroutines, `calls++` is a data race. The exact-count assertion would also be flaky, because other goroutines may report progress before they see the cancellation.
findings.suggestion: Use an `atomic.Int32` for the counter. Assert `calls >= 1` unless `computeTolerance` documents that progress is always reported serially on the calling goroutine.
findings.evidence: _, err := computeTolerance(ctx, v.Result.Source, p, func(int) { calls++; cancel() })

findings.title: Unchecked column index in CSV assertion can panic
findings.message: `rows[1][5]` is read without checking how many columns the row has. `csv.Reader` with default settings rejects rows whose field count differs from the header, but a header with fewer than 6 columns would still pass. In that case the test panics with an index-out-of-range instead of failing with a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Check `len(rows[1]) > 5` before indexing, or locate the failure column by its header name.
